paper.title: Asymptotically Optimal Sequential Design for Rank Aggregation

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential design for rank aggregation (Bayesian decision framework)
unmapped: Goal is to output a full ranking of K items; loss = Kendall's tau distance + c * (number of comparisons), with the learner choosing its stopping time (Bayes risk, asymptotics as c -> 0)
General parametric pairwise comparison model f_theta^a (e.g. BTL, Thurstone) with latent scores theta, theta_1 = 0
Learner knows the sampling cost c and the support W of the prior
settings.definition_quote: a decision maker is responsible for ranking $K$ items by adaptively collecting noisy outcome of pairwise comparison from judges. ... The Bayes risk combines the risks associated with Kendall's tau distance of the decision and the sampling cost, V_c(\rho,\pi) = E^{\pi}(L_K(\{R_{i,j}\})+L_c(T))

algorithms.name: Sequential Ranking Policy pi_1 = (A_p, T_1, R) (epsilon-greedy Chernoff-type selection, sum-type GLR stopping)
Sequential Ranking Policy pi_2 = (A_p, T_2, R) (epsilon-greedy Chernoff-type selection, min-type GLR stopping)

symbols.E_t_c: E[t_c(Theta)] = integral of |log c|/D(theta) rho(theta) dtheta, D(theta) the max-min weighted KL characteristic

conditions: Assumptions A1-A5: compact prior support with nonempty interior per ranking, regular support, smooth log-likelihood, indifference zone (no ties), prior density bounded above and below

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:compact}-\ref{assump:prior}, we have \liminf_{c\to 0}\frac{{V}^*_c(\rho)}{c\EE t_c(\Theta)}\geq 1, where $\EE t_c(\Theta)= \int_W t_c(\ttt)\rho(\ttt)d\ttt$.

results.notes: Lower bound on the minimal Bayes risk (expected Kendall tau + c*E[T]); quantity 'other'. Ratio lower bound recorded as liminf with expression c*E t_c.

tuning: pair selection rule satisfies A6: min_{t,(i,j)} lambda_t^{i,j} >= |log c|^{-1/2+delta_0}

source.label: thm:error
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:compact}-\ref{assump:prior} and Assumption~\ref{assump:identifiability}, we consider a policy $\pi_i=(A,T_i,{R})$ ($i=1,2$), where $A$ is a pair selection rule satisfying Assumption~\ref{assump:randomized} ... Then, $\EE L_K(\{R_{i,j}\})=O(c) \mbox{ for } i=1,2.$

results.notes: Expected (Bayes-averaged) Kendall's tau error. Holds for both T_1 and T_2 with any selection rule satisfying A6; attached to pi_2 (same bound for pi_1).

tuning: selection rule satisfies A6 (min selection prob >= |log c|^{-1/2+delta_0}) and A8 (adopted lambda_n converges to hat lambda_n uniformly as c -> 0)

source.label: thm:stopping-time
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:compact}-\ref{assump:prior} and Assumption~\ref{assump:identifiability}, we consider the policy $\pi=(A,T_i,{R})$ ($i=1,2$). If the pair assignment rule $A$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assump:randomized} and~\ref{assump:optimal}, then $\limsup_{c\to 0}\frac{\EE T_i}{\EE t_c(\Theta)} \leq 1 ~~(i=1,2).$

results.notes: Bayes-averaged expected stopping time; holds for both T_1 and T_2.

source.label: cor:opt
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:compact}-\ref{assump:prior}, and Assumption~\ref{assump:identifiability}, if we choose $p\propto |\log c|^{-\frac{1}{2}+\delta_0}$ for some $\delta_0$ satisfying $0<\delta_0<\frac{1}{2}$, then $\pi_i=(A_p,T_i,R)$, $i=1,2$ are asymptotically optimal policies.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality: Bayes risk V_c(rho,pi_i) = (1+o(1)) c E t_c(Theta), matching Theorem 1. Holds for both pi_1 and pi_2.
